title: Work, energy and power

parts.text:
16 A hydroelectric power station uses the gravitational potential energy of water to generate
electrical energy.
In one particular power station, the mass of water flowing per unit time is 1.5  105
kg s–1. The
water falls through a vertical height of 120 m.
The electrical power generated is 100 MW.
What is the efficiency of the power station?
A
5.6%
B
43%
C
57%
D
77%

hints: Notice the water supply is given as mass per unit time, $1.5 \times 10^5 \text{ kg s}^{-1}$, falling $120 \text{ m}$, so work out the gravitational energy lost per second.
Recall input power is rate of loss of $mgh$ and efficiency is $\text{useful output power} / \text{total input power}$, with $100 \text{ MW} = 100 \times 10^6 \text{ W}$.
Calculate $(\text{mass per second}) \times g \times h$ to get about $1.77 \times 10^8 \text{ W}$, then divide $100 \text{ MW}$ by this input and multiply by $100%$.
walkthrough: Identify the input and output: input is gravitational potential energy lost per second by $1.5 \times 10^5 \text{ kg s}^{-1}$ falling $120 \text{ m}$, output is $100 \text{ MW} = 100 \times 10^6 \text{ W}$.
State the rules: input power $P_{in} = \text{energy per second} = (mgh)/t = (m/t)gh$, and efficiency $= P_{out}/P_{in}$.
Substitute with units: $P_{in} = (1.5 \times 10^5 \text{ kg s}^{-1})(9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2})(120 \text{ m})$.
Calculate the intermediate result: $P_{in} = 1.5 \times 10^5 \times 1177.2 \text{ W} \approx 1.77 \times 10^8 \text{ W} = 177 \text{ MW}$.
Find efficiency: $\text{efficiency} = (100 \times 10^6)/(177 \times 10^6) \approx 0.565$, or about $57%$ after multiplying by $100%$. This is option C.

A.explanation: Too small by a factor of 10, from an error in powers of 10 when converting $100 \text{ MW}$ and $1.5 \times 10^5 \text{ kg s}^{-1}$ to watts and input power.

B.explanation: Less than the true ratio of $100 \text{ MW}$ to the gravitational input power of about $177 \text{ MW}$.

C.explanation: Equals $100 \text{ MW}$ divided by the input power $(1.5 \times 10^5 \times 9.81 \times 120) \text{ W}$, about $57%$.

D.explanation: Too large, greater than the ratio of useful electrical power $100 \text{ MW}$ to the available gravitational power.
